history.content: What is more beautiful out of the California juniper and the Cheese bush?
I do not have specific information on whether the California juniper or the Cheese bush is more beautiful, as beauty is subjective and can vary from person to person.
Exactly so!  what is cheese bush anyway?

Cheese bush is a plant species native to California. It is typically found in areas north of Rosamond. Why we find a concentration of these wayward shrubs in the State Park is a mystery.  I do not have detailed descriptions for the shrub.
Talking about juniper, how do you know male and female?

The male trees produce tiny cones, while the female trees produce berries. Some juniper trees, like the California juniper, can even change sex each year. For example, a juniper tree on the Rare Juniper Trail appeared to have been changing sex when it had both male cones and female berries. Now, it only has male cones.  Also, in this woodland, there are about nine trees prolifically producing berries, with this one producing the most earning it the nickname "Big Mama." In winter, male cones and female reactors form. Wind distributes the pollen, and the berries that form in March and April will stay on the tree until August or September of the following year. So, between March and August of any year there will be two berry crops on the trees simultaneously.

The shapes of California junipers can vary. Some have a more spreading shape, while others are more upright. The "Big Mama" juniper specimen has 15 trunks, giving it a unique shape.   A seedling of a California juniper has a single trunk. Typically, the seedlings form a "burl" at the base from which multiple tree trunks then grow. Most of the junipers have 2 - 12 trunks.
what is the other tree that is very famous in CA...do you remember?

One of the most famous tree species in California is the coast redwood. These trees are known for their impressive height and age, the largest one is approximately 277 feet tall and about 1,500 years old.
